 EFSC Cyber Titans Earn Third Place in Statewide Cybersecurity Competition
October 26, 2026 
 Eastern Florida State College's Cyber Titans cybersecurity team has earned third place
 in the Fourth Annual Florida College System Cybersecurity Competition, demonstrating
 the technical expertise and problem-solving skills that are preparing students for
 careers in one of the nation's fastest-growing fields.
 The Cyber Titans finished among the top cybersecurity teams in Florida, earning third
 place overall in competition with 17 colleges from across the state in a challenging
 virtual cyber range environment designed to replicate real-world cyber threats and
 incidents.
 The Cyber Titans Team included Jason Beck, Ryan Bryant, Andrew Klinsic, and Christen
 Stone.
 Led by Nicole Dyess, EFSC assistant professor of Advanced Technology and Computer
 Science and manager of the EFSC Center for Cyber Security and Digital Forensics, the
 team successfully identified, analyzed, and responded to complex cybersecurity challenges
 during the statewide competition, which was hosted by the Florida College System as
 part of Cybersecurity Awareness Month.
 "This achievement reflects the hard work, dedication, and talent of our Cyber Titans
 students," said Dyess. "Cybersecurity requires critical thinking, teamwork, and the
 ability to respond under pressure. Our students demonstrated all of those qualities
 while competing against outstanding teams from across Florida."
 The competition challenged students to detect, respond to, and mitigate cyber threats
 through realistic simulations that tested their ability to manage and defend network
 infrastructures while making decisions in high-pressure scenarios like those encountered
 by cybersecurity professionals.
 Florida remains the only state in the nation with a systemwide college cybersecurity
 competition of its kind. This year's event featured 17 teams representing institutions
 across the Florida College System.
 “We are extremely proud of EFSC’s Cyber Titans led by Assistant Professor Nicole Dyess,”
 said College President Dr. Jim Richey. “Earning a Top 3 spot in the state in this
 highly competitive event is something which all Titans should be proud. This highly
 challenging competition showcases Florida's very best. Just to compete at a high level
 is an honor much less being recognized as one of the best programs in Florida, a state
 recognized for leading the nation in workforce education. This latest success is one
 more example of the commitment of our faculty to prepare students for high-demand
 careers that meet the needs of employers on the Space Coast.”
 In addition to the competition, students participated in professional development
 opportunities alongside technology leaders from across Florida. The event included
 sessions focused on industry trends, workforce needs, and emerging cybersecurity challenges
 facing the state and nation.
 All participants received a cyber range certification from Global Business Solutions,
 Inc. Winning teams were evaluated on their ability to efficiently operate, manage,
 and defend network infrastructures across multiple simulated organizations.
 The Florida College System Cybersecurity Competition supports the mission of the Florida
 College System Cybersecurity Collaborative, which brings together cybersecurity leaders
 from Florida's public colleges to strengthen workforce partnerships, expand opportunities
 for students, and advance cybersecurity education statewide.
 For more information about Eastern Florida State College's cybersecurity programs,
 visit easternflorida.edu or call 321-632-1111.
